title: Close an attached-lid tote: lower both lids together so the lips along their seam seat flush
instruction: Close the lids of the tote.
context: O*NET 53-7065.00, Stockers and Order Fillers: 2,804,300 US employees in 2025 (BLS data as shown on O*NET). Two of its core tasks are "Pack and unpack items to be stocked on shelves in stockrooms, warehouses, or storage yards." and "Receive, unload, open, unpack, or issue sales floor merchandise." Closing a tote's lids is part of that handling, not a separately listed task.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); one fixed layout matching the screenshot (the screenshot is a render-only view from the far side of the table, looking back toward the arms: the whole tote, both lids and both supports are visible, with the part of each support's top under its lid hidden; the arm bases are out of the picture). Arm bases: x 0, y +30.5 cm (left arm) and y -30.5 cm (right arm), on the table surface. Tote: one Akro-Mils 39085 attached-lid container (akro-mils.com/product/attached-lid-container-39085/), blue plastic, catalogue outside size 21.5 x 15 x 9 in (54.6 x 38.1 x 22.9 cm at the rim band), 1.9 kg (estimated), standing loose on its base, long side along x, at its mark (the tote is not fixed; sliding it is scored); the mark is the outline of the tote's base, taped on the table (49.6 x 33.1 cm, 2.5 cm inside the rim outline on every side), centred at x 52, y 0. Two lids. Lid length, hinge offset, knuckle count and all lid-feature sizes are estimated from product photos. Each lid is a 53.8 cm long, 0.4 cm thick plate (estimated) of the same plastic, 0.4 kg (estimated), hinged on the two long sides (axes 0.4 cm outside the rim band) with 7 hinge knuckles per side. Each lid has two bosses (2.4 cm diameter, 0.3 cm proud, on its top face 8 cm from the hinge axis and 14 cm either side of the lid's middle), a 5 x 3 x 0.7 cm stacking lug at each outer corner on the hinge side, and a 2 x 2.5 x 0.8 cm seal block with a 0.6 cm hole at each end of its seam edge (hole seen in the grey retailer image). Hinge range (estimated): 0 (closed) to 265 degrees. Real lids hang about 270 degrees against the outside of the long wall (manufacturer's video, https://youtu.be/B8cnZ48xBc0, and a maker's product image of four totes, two with their lids open and hanging), so each trial starts with both lids lying flat outward (180 degrees, top faces down), each on a fixed support, its near end (x 25.1 cm) overhanging the support by 10 cm. Supports (not part of the product): two plywood boxes or stacked lumber, each 38.4 cm long (x 35.1 to 73.5 cm) and 13.0 cm wide (y +31.5 to +44.5 cm under the left lid, y -44.5 to -31.5 cm under the right lid), with a flat top 22.46 cm above the table (the design height), taped to the table at their marks. The tops carry each lid's flat top face beyond its bosses (2 cm clear) and logo plates and stay clear of its lugs and seal blocks; they extend 2.5 cm or more past the lid's outer edge. Level check: shim each support until a digital inclinometer (or phone level app), zeroed on the table beside the tote, reads 0.0 +- 0.3 degrees on the lid's upward face (its underside, since the lid lies top face down) with the lid resting on the support. Seam (estimated from product photos of the closed lids, about +-1.5 cm; tops flush with a 0.2 cm gap): a polyline of (x, y) points in cm from the tote's centre, y positive to the left: (-26.9, +3.0), (-21.5, +3.0), (-15.8, -3.0), (-3.0, -3.0), (3.0, +3.0), (15.8, +3.0), (21.5, -3.0), (26.9, -3.0): four straight runs joined by three diagonals, each lid having one long and one short straight stretch of edge reaching across the centre line. Lap: product images show each lid's edge alternating between a raised lip and a lower shelf along the seam (observed); the 4 mm step, thicknesses, lap lengths and which lid has the upper lip where are estimated, and that neither lid can be shut alone follows from the images and is confirmed by a team member's first-hand experience; in the model the second lid rests on the first lid's upper lip. The model has no snap or latch; a shut lid is held by its weight. In the seller's product video (https://www.amazon.ca/vdp/09c3c1c46a40487390129b9b26503d1c, about 0:19-0:25, clearest from about 0:20) the team sees both lids being shut at the same time. Both arms start in the rig's ready pose (joint angles 0.0, 1.0, 1.0, -0.6, 0.0, 0.0 rad for joints 1 to 6), grippers open.
scoring: Tools: tape measure, digital inclinometer (or phone level app; accuracy about +-0.2 degrees, an estimate), video. 0 for the whole trial if the tote ever slides more than 3 cm from its mark (the outline of its base on the table) or tilts more than 10 degrees from its starting reading (two-axis inclinometer or phone level app taped to the tote's end wall, zeroed on the table before the trial, read from video; the supports are fixed and not scored). A lid is seated when the tilt of its top face across its width (hinge side to seam side) is below 0.5 degrees from horizontal, read with the inclinometer placed on a flat part of the lid top at the lid's measuring point (avoid the logo plates), after zeroing it on the table beside the tote so that table tilt cancels. The reading is taken without pressing on the lid. A lid open 90 degrees or more is never seated. Optional visual check, not scored: when both lids are seated their top faces are flush across the seam. In the model this is the same definition, not a second one: free-edge height u*sin(theta) below 2.0 mm at u = 22.45 cm from the hinge axis, which is 0.51 degrees. 0.5 degrees separates a seated lid (0.0 degrees in the model) from a lid resting on the other lid's lip (1.4 degrees in the model, 5.5 mm at the measuring point). Measuring points, x from the tote's centre: x -9.4 cm for the left lid and x +9.4 cm for the right lid; each is the middle of the 12.8 cm straight stretch of that lid's edge that reaches farthest across the centre line (x -15.8 to -3.0 cm on the left lid, x +3.0 to +15.8 cm on the right lid). If your reading of the photos is mirrored, this feature definition governs, not the x values. A lid is down when it is open less than 10 degrees. Score 1.0 if, at the end of the run, both lids have been seated, still (no visible motion of either lid for 2 s of video; in the model, hinge speed under 0.05 rad/s) and both grippers 3 cm or more from the tote (tape measure from the tool point, midway between the fingertips, to the closed tote's outline: a box 54.6 x 38.1 cm up to the top of the seal blocks, 24.1 cm above the table) for the last 2 s (the run stops as soon as this first holds). Otherwise the final state decides, and only if both grippers are 3 cm or more from the tote (else 0): 0.75 if both lids are seated; 0.5 if one lid is seated and the other down but not seated (as when it rests on the first lid's upper lip); 0.25 if exactly one lid is seated (the other open 10 degrees or more), or both are down and neither is seated; 0 in every other case. A real trial is scored on the final settled state.
reset_notes: Put the tote on its mark (the taped outline of its base) and both supports on theirs (nothing else is moved by a trial; the supports are fixed). Lay both lids flat outward, top faces down, each on its support with its near end overhanging 10 cm; the lids do not stay flat by themselves, and a lid let go anywhere else swings down and hangs. Check each lid's support as in setup (inclinometer, zeroed on the table, reading 0.0 +- 0.3 degrees on the lid's underside, across its width on a flat part of the underside between x 40 and 70 cm). Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid tub, lids, supports; one damped hinge per lid (0 to 265 deg); no flex. Estimated from product photos: wall, rim, thicknesses, masses, hinge stop, seam polyline, bosses, lugs. Alternating lip/shelf seam sections are from product images; lap sizes and which lid has the upper lip where are estimated; closing-order jam: images plus a first-hand account. Ribs not modelled. Real lids hang ~270 deg; trials start on supports. Model: second lid rests 1.4 deg open (5.5 mm) on the first's lip.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (1,800 steps, no lid closed); demo: 1.0
